questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kosi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kosi is known as the **'Sorrow of Bihar'.**
 
• Kosi River:
 
 
• These include the Tamur Koshi originating from the Kanchenjunga area in the east, the Arun River from Tibet, and Sun Koshi from the Gosainthan area farther west. The Sun Koshi's tributaries from east to west are Dudh Koshi, Bhote Koshi, Tamba Koshi, and Indravati Koshi. 
 
• The sources of seven streams of the Kosi are located in snow-covered areas which also receive heavy rainfall.
 
 
• Consequently, a huge volume of water flows with tremendous speed.
 
 
 
• They unite at Triveni north of the Mahabharata Range to form the Kosi.
 
• The river enters the Tarai of Nepal after cutting a narrow gorge in the Mahabharata Range.
 
• The river channel is braided and it shifts its course frequently.
 
• This has resulted in frequent devastating floods and has converted large tracts of cultivable land into the wasteland in Bihar.
 
 
• **Hence, the Kosi River is often referred to as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.**​
 
 
 
 

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/917ccc7ffa6d7421b062ae08dddf8b091f383585bd136bb1b1421dc5ede8de80.png] **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The Koshi is 720 km (450 mi) long and drains an area of about 74,500 km2 (28,800 sq mi) in Tibet, Nepal, and Bihar.
 
• A review of 28 historical maps from 1760 to 1960 found that there was a slight eastward change in river course over a long period and that the shift was random and oscillatory in nature.
 
• During a flood, the average water flow (discharge) increases up to 18 times the average.
 
• As the annual floods affect about 21,000 km2 (8,100 sq mi) of fertile agricultural lands thereby disturbing the rural economy. Hence, the Kosi River is often referred to as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.
 
• The Kosi river **joins the Ganges at Kursela in the Katihar** district of Bihar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **sorrow of Bengal **is the **Damodar River.**
 
• The **sorrow of Odisha** is the **Mahanadi river.**
 
• The **sorrow of Assam** is the **Brahmaputra river.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **In News__**

 
• **Dagmara Hydro Energy Project**

 
 
• It will be built **on the Kosi river.**
 
• An MoU has been signed between NHPC Limited and Bihar State Hydroelectric Power Corporation Limited (BSHPC) for the implementation of the **130.1 Megawatt (MW)** Dagmara HE Project in** Supaul, Bihar.**
 
 
 
• **Kosi Rail Mahasety (Mega Bridge)**
 
 
• ​Inaugurated by - PM Narendra Modi
 
• Length - 1.9 km
 
• Connecting - Mithila and Kosi region
 
• It reduces the rail distance between Nirmali and Saraigarh from the present 298 Km to 22 Km.
 
 

4d:T

questions.question: In which of the following places did the Indian National Congress hold its special session in September 1920?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Congress held a **special session** in **Calcutta **in **September 1920** under the presidentship of **Lala Lajpat Rai.**
 
• It met to pass the resolution of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi wrongly predicted that if the non-cooperation movement gets successful, Swaraj could be attained in one year.
 
• The Non-cooperation movement was launched in 1920 by Mahatma Gandhi with the aim of Swaraj (self-governance). However, the movement was not successful.
 
• **Non-cooperation program approved by the Congress at a special session in Calcutta in September 1920, included:**
 
 
• Boycott of government schools and colleges.
 
• Boycott of law courts and dispensation of justice through panchayats instead.
 
• Boycott of legislative councils.
 
• Boycott of foreign cloth and use of khadi instead; also practice of hand-spinning to be done.
 
• Renunciation of government honors and titles.
 
• The second phase could include mass civil disobedience including resignation from government service, and non-payment of taxes. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• The normal session of congress was held from 26 to 30 December **1920 **in **Nagpur **under the presidentship of **C. Vijayaraghavachariar.**

questions.question: Any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than ______ years is under the category of Culturable Wasteland.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Culturable wasteland** refers to the land which is **not cultivated for more than five years in sequence**.
 
• This land has the potential to grow crops but was left unused for any reason.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fallow land**__

 __
 
• This includes land which was taken up for cultivation but is** temporarily out of cultivation** for a period of **not less than one year and not more than five years.**
 
 
 
• **Unculturable land**__
 
 
• This includes all land covered by mountains, deserts, etc.
 
• This land cannot be brought under cultivation except at an exorbitant cost and is classified as unculturable land.

questions.question: ______ of the Indian Constitution contains the Fundamental Duties.
Alexander the Great defeated Porus in the Battle of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydaspes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Alexander the Great defeated Porus in the Battle of Hydaspes.

 
 
• The Battle is called the “Battle of Hydaspes” named after the Hydaspes (Jhelum) River in Greek.
 
 
 
• The battle was fought in 326 BC with the king of the Paurava dynasty, located on the banks of the Vitasta (Jhelum) river in the **Punjab region.**
 
• In 326 BC, Alexander invaded India, after crossing the river Indus he advanced towards Taxila.
 
• He then challenged king Porus, ruler of the Paurava kingdom, between the rivers Jhelum and Chenab.
 
• The fight on the banks of the Hydaspes River in India was the closest Alexander the Great came to defeat. His feared companion cavalry was unable to subdue fully the courageous King Porus.
 
• The forces were numerically quite evenly balanced, although Alexander had more cavalry and Porus fielded 200 war elephants.
 
• Following the battle, King Porus was brought before Alexander and was asked how he wished to be treated, Porus replied “Treat me as a king would treat another king”. Impressed, Alexander indeed treated him like a king, allowing him to retain his lands.
 
• In **326 BC**, the army of Alexander approached the boundaries of the Nanda Empire. His army, exhausted from the continuous campaigning and concerned at the prospect of facing yet another gigantic Indian army, demanded that they should return to the west. This happened at the Hyphasis (modern Beas).​

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alexander**

 
 
• He was the king of Macedonia and was popularly known as Alexander the Great.
 
• He was a member of the Argead dynasty and was born in 356 BC.
 
• He succeeded his father, Philip, to the throne of Macedonia at the age of only 20.
 
• He quickly conquered many areas including the **Persian (Iranian) empire.**
 
 
 
• After the Battle of Hydaspes and the resounding victory of his troops at Sakla, he reached the Beas River.
 
• But his** soldiers refused to go further,** as they were afraid of the great Magadha kingdom across the Beas river.
 
• **At that time **the Magadha kingdom was ruled by the **Nanda dynasty and the ruler of the Nanda dynasty was Dhanananda**.
 
 
• Mahapadma Nanda was the founder of the Nanda dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Alexander** marched back and reached **Babylon in 323 BC, where he died at the age of 33.**

questions.question: According to the Census of 2011, which of the following is the third most populated urban agglomeration?

questions.question: For which of the following media is the absolute refractive index almost equal to one?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Air.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refractive Index** of a medium: 

 
 
• It tells the **capacity** of the **medium to bend a light ray** when it passes through.
 
• The Refractive index is **inversely proportional to the speed of the light.**
 
• It is a dimensionless quantity.
 
 
 
• **The absolute refractive index** of a medium:
 
 
• It is expressed as the **ratio speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in the medium.**
 
• It is a comparison of the speeds of light of different media.
 
• The speed of light in air is almost equal to the speed of light in a vacuum. So, absolute refractive index, μ = c / c = 1.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **Medium**
 **Absolute Refractive index**
 
 

 Vacuum
 1
 
 

 Air
 1.007
 
 

 Ice
 1.31
 
 

 Water
 1.33
 
 

 Kerosene
 1.44

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a disease caused by bacteria?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaria.**__

__**Explanation:**__

**Option 1: Dysentery**

__
 
• It is an infection in the intestines.
 
• 
 
It can be caused by protozoa (*Entamoeba histolytica)* or bacteria (*Shigella).*

 

**Option 2: Diphtheria**

 
• It affects the mucous membranes of the nose and throat.
 
• It is a highly contagious disease.
 
• 
 
Pathogen: ***Corynebacterium diphtheriae (Bacteria)***

 

**Option 3: Malaria**

 
• Malaria is caused by ***Plasmodium.***
 
• 
 
***Plasmodium*** is a genus of parasitic protozoans.

 

**Option 4:** **Plague**

 
• It is a bacterial infectious disease.
 
• Pathogen: ***Yersinia Pestis *****(Bacteria)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Different species of ***Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. malaria, and P. falciparum)*** are responsible for different types of malaria. 
 
• 
 
Plasmodium falciparum is the most serious one and can even be fatal.

 
 
• 
 
***Plasmodium*** enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. 

 
 
• 
 
The parasites initially multiply within the liver cells and then attack the **red blood cells (RBCs)** resulting in their rupture.

 
 
• 
 
So, the correct answer is** option 3.**

questions.question: Which Amendment Act (2017) of the Constitution contains the provisions necessary for the GST Regime?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**101st**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India,** GST Bill was first introduced in 2014 as The Constitution (122nd Amendment) Bill**.
 
• This got approval in 2016 and was renumbered in the statute by Rajya Sabha as **The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016**.
 
• **The provisions of The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016** :
 
 
• Central GST to cover Excise duty, Service tax, etc, State GST to cover VAT, luxury tax, etc.
 
• Integrated GST to cover inter-state trade. 
 
• Article 246A – states have the power to tax goods and services.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• Article 279A provided the formation of the GST Council by the President to administer & govern GST.
 
• Its Chairman is the Union Finance Minister of India with ministers nominated by the state governments as its members.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**

 
 
• It is a value-added tax levied on most goods and services sold for domestic consumption.
 
• The GST is paid by consumers, but it is remitted to the government by the businesses selling the goods and services.

questions.question: Gaumukh Kund is a reservoir located in which of the following forts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittorgarh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaumukh Kund** is a sacred water body situated on the western part of the famous **Chittorgarh Fort. **
 
• 'Gaumukh' literally means the** 'mouth of a cow'.** The water flows through the cracks in the rocks and in due course, falls into the reservoir.
 
• The Chittorgarh Fort **is also known as** **Chittorgarh or Chittor Fort.**
 
• Chittorgarh Fort is the largest fort in India and Asia.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site.**
 
• The fort used to be the **capital of Mewar rulers.**
 
• It is **located in** the present-day town of **Chittorgarh in Rajasthan.**
 
• Built-in the 7th century AD, Chittorgarh Fort has withstood three major Muslim invasions starting from Alauddin Khilji in 1303, in 1535 by Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, and in 1568 by Akbar.

 
• It is situated on the bank of Berach river (Banas River tributary).
 
• Chittorgarh Fort has a total of seven gates and the main gate is named the Ram Pol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98b862fde257d6b28c87df75978a0762ad5aa7a34906b381410c669e3edf201b.png] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Kumbhalgarh Fort:

 
 
• **Kumbhalgarh Fort** is located in the Rajsamand district of **Rajasthan.**
 
• Built by **Rana Kumbha **from the Sisodia Rajput dynasty.
 
• Longwall of the 36-kilometer length makes it the great wall of India.
 
• A special attraction in the fort is the Lakhola tank, Ganesh temple, and Parsvanatha temple.
 
• Kumbhalgarh is well known as the birthplace of Maharana Pratap.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior Fort**
 
 
• Gwalior Fort is known as Gibraltar of India.
 
• It was given the name ”The Perl in the necklace of the forts of Hind” by Mughal Emperor Babur.
 
• It was built in 525 AD century and it is one of the biggest forts in India.
 
• It was built by Suraj Sen.
 
• Temple Teli-ka-mandir is the most famous temple constructed in the Dravidian style of temple architecture.
 
 
 
• **Datia Mahal**
 
 
• Datia Mahal is a 7-storied architecture with two floors positioned in the basement.
 
• It is only made out of stone and bricks without any usage of wood or iron. So, the whole 7- storied building stands without any support of metal or even wood. 
 
• Datia Mahal is one of the great examples of Indo-Islamic architecture in India. A blend of Rajputana and Mughal styles gives it a luxurious look.

questions.question: The Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were set up in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1857**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Universities of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras were set up in 1857.**

 
 
• **​**The Governor-General of India at that time was **Lord Canning.**
 
 
 
• After the recommendation of wood's dispatch, these universities were formed.
 
• The Universities of **Calcutta and Bombay (now Mumbai) were formed in July 1857 **and **Madras (now Chennai) in September 1857**, followed by** Punjab in 1882, and Allahabad University in 1887.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

__
 
• Wood's Dispatch:__

 
 
• Sir **Charles Wood`s Dispatch of 1854, **famously known as the **‘Magna Carta of English Education in India’.**
 
• It recommended creating a properly articulated scheme of education from primary school to the university.
 
• It sought to** encourage indigenous education **and planned the formulation of a coherent policy of education.
 
• In, 1854 he sent a despatch about the new norms of education to that time Governor-General of India Lord Dalhousie.
 
• It was recommended that Universities would be working on the model of the London University be established in **b****ig **cities of India such as Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay. **Hence, these universities were formed.**

questions.question: ______ is a famous dance form of Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dumhal.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dumhal**__

 __
 
• **The Dumhal dance is one of the most prominent folk dances in Jammu & Kashmir, India**.
 
• In the Wattal tribe, the Dumhal dance is performed on certain occasions.
 
• The dancers' tunes are folk melodies that they sing in a chorus.
 
• The men hold a banner, gather in a procession, and march to a designated area.
 
• They arrive at a specific area and plant the flag on the earth.
 
• The Dumhal dance is then performed which revolves around the banner.
 
• **This dance is said to have been created by Shah Sukar Saloni, a devout follower of a Sufi saint known as "Baba Nasim-U-Din-Gazi."**
 
• Shah Sukar created this dance form to honor the Sufi saint.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dhemsa is a traditional folk dance of tribal people of central India-Southern **Odisha **and adjacent areas of **Chhattisgarh **and** Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The Dance form **Bidesia **is very renowned among the locals in the state, **Bihar**. It is considered the most popular folk dance of Bihar.
 
• **Karma dance** which is also popularly known as **Karma Naachis performed by the tribes of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Orissa and other regions of the country.**

questions.question: 26 November was formally declared as the Constitution Day on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**19 November 2015.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **26 November was formally declared as the Constitution Day on 19 November 2015.**
 
• Constitution Day, also known as National Law Day, is observed annually on 26 November.
 
 
• Because, before this, the day was observed as National Law Day.
 
• **Dr. Ambedkar** was** the first Law Minister of India.**
 
 
 
• The day marks the **adoption of the Indian Constitution** by the **Constituent Assembly in 1949.**
 
• The provisions relating to **citizenship, elections, provisional parliament, and temporary and transitional provisions** were given immediate effect from **November 26, 1949.**
 
• The **whole Constitution** became effective **on 26 January 1950** marking the beginning of a new era in the history of the Indian Republic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Indian Constitution**__

 
 
• It is the **longest written constitution** in the world.
 
• It was **framed and given to themselves by the people of India** and was** adopted by the Constituent Assembly**.
 
• The **first meeting of the Constituent Assembly** was presided by** Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha**.
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was elected the President of the Constituent Assembly on** December 11, 1946**.
 
• **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** was the **chairman of the Drafting Committee.**
 
• Constituent Assembly held **11 sessions and took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to frame the Constitution**.
 
 
 
• The Constitution as originally adopted contained **22 parts, 395 articles, and 8 schedules.**

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT figure among the Five Kingdom Classification proposed by RH Whittaker (1969)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Euglena.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The five-kingdom classification was proposed by R.H. Whittaker in **1969.**
 
• The main criteria for classification used by him:
 
 
• (1) Cell structure (2) Body organization (3) Mode of nutrition (4) Reproduction (5) Phylogenetic relationships.
 
 
 
• The five-kingdom defined by him:
 
 
• Monera - All the prokarytotes
 
• Protista - All the Unicellular eukaryotes
 
• Fungi - True fungi
 
• Plantae - All the multicellular plants
 
• Animalia - All the multicellular animals 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://qph.fs.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-8f4359dec7b955dd5f5eda2522e8e4f6] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Euglena is a genus of **single-cell flagellate eukaryotes.**
 
• It is the best-known and most widely studied member of the class **Euglenoidea,** a diverse group containing at least 800 species.
 
• Species of Euglena are found in **fresh water and saltwater.** 
 
• It is unique as it is both heterotrophic (must consume food) and autotrophic (can make its own food) in nature.
 
• It is also known as green protozoa.

questions.question: Arunima Sinha was the first ______ female to scale Mount Everest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __female amputee.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Arunima Sinha was the world's first female **amputee **to scale Mount Everest.
 
• She was also the world's first female amputee to scale Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount Elbrus, Mount Kosciusko, Mount Aconcagua, Carstensz Pyramid, and Mount Vinson.
 
• Arunima Sinha was awarded the Padma Shri award in 2015 and Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award in 2015.
 
• She was also awarded the First Lady Award in 2016, Malala Award, Yash Bharti Award, Rani Laxmi Bai Award, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1984.
 
• Santosh Yadav is the first woman in the world to climb **Mount Everest rest twice**, and the **first woman to successfully climb Mount Everest from** **Kangshung Face.**
 
• Premlata Agrawal is the first Indian woman to scale the Seven Summits, the seven highest continental peaks of the world.

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'A Passage to India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**EM Forster.**__

__***Key Points__**

__
 
• A Passage to India* (1924) is a novel by English author E. M. Forster set against the backdrop of the British Raj and the Indian independence movement in the 1920s.
 
• It was selected as one of the 100 great works of 20th-century English literature by the *Modern Library* and won the 1924 James Tait Black Memorial Prize for fiction.
 
• Time magazine included the novel in its "All Time 100 Novels" list.
 
• The novel is based on Forster's experiences in India, deriving the title from **Walt Whitman's 1870 poem "Passage to India"** in *Leaves of Grass*.
 
• The story revolves around four characters: Dr Aziz, his British friend Mr Cyril Fielding, Mrs Moore, and Miss Adela Quested.
 
• During a trip to the fictitious Marabar Caves (modeled on the Barabar Caves of Bihar), Adela thinks she finds herself alone with Dr Aziz in one of the caves (when in fact he is in an entirely different cave), and subsequently panics and flees; it is assumed that Dr Aziz has attempted to assault her.
 
• Aziz's trial, and its run-up and aftermath, bring to a boil the common racial tensions and prejudices between Indians and the British who rule India.
